target.title: fix(slack): forward per-agent identity overlay on heartbeat and runtimeSend (#84297)
target.body: ## Summary Per-agent Slack identity (`agents.list[].identity`) doesn't survive the heartbeat / announce path. Two things go wrong: 1. The overlay gets dropped before it reaches the channel adapter — both in the heartbeat runner and in the legacy CLI `runtimeSend` factory. 2. Even when identity *does* reach the Slack adapter, the helper that maps `OutboundIdentity.emoji` → `chat.postMessage.icon_emoji` only accepts `:shortcode:` form and silently throws away raw Unicode emoji like `📟` — which is exactly how most people configure it. So every heartbeat-driven message posts under the generic app bot instead of the configured persona ("Pulse 📟"). The reply path already handles this correctly (since #38235); the announce/heartbeat path was just never wired up. **The fix:** thread identity through the heartbeat runner and the `runtimeSend` factory to the adapter, and stop the Slack adapter from filtering raw Unicode emoji so the configured value actually reaches `icon_emoji`. **What changed:** - Added `RuntimeSendOpts.identity?: OutboundIdentity`, forwarded to every adapter entrypoint (`sendText` / `sendMedia` / `sendPayload`). - The heartbeat runner resolves the agent's identity once (`resolveAgentOutboundIdentity(cfg, agentId)`, right next to `outboundSession`) and passes it into both `sendDurableMessageBatch` calls. - `resolveSlackSendIdentity` in `extensions/slack/src/outbound-adapter.ts` now passes `identity.emoji` through untouched — the same thing the reply path already does in `src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts`. - Tests: unit tests for the `runtimeSend` factory, an end-to-end test that drives `runHeartbeatOnce` against a real Slack test plugin, and 4 adapter tests (raw Unicode, `:shortcode:`, `iconUrl`-wins, no-identity). **Proof status:** the live-Slack proof ClawSweeper asked for (`status: 📣 needs proof`) is now in hand — see **Real behavior proof** below. The reporter (@aw-stevens), who runs the affected `chat:write.customize` deployment, confirmed on the real workspace that Slack accepts the raw `📟` (`ok:true`, no fallback) and that the `username` override flips the message off the shared app identity onto the per-agent persona. **What this PR deliberately leaves alone:** the cron `--announce` path. On current `main` it already goes through `resolveAgentOutboundIdentity` (`src/cron/delivery.ts`, lines 68 / 105). The reporter's original trace was against the v2026.5.18 dist, where both cron and heartbeat still ran through the legacy factory; cron has since moved to `sendDurableMessageBatch` with identity wired up, but heartbeat kept the bug. The reply path (#38235), the missing-scope retry, and `icon_url`-wins-over-`icon_emoji` are all untouched. ## Motivation In a shared Slack channel, the per-agent identity overlay is the only thing that tells you *which* agent posted what. Without it, every cron digest and every heartbeat push from every agent shows up under one generic app bot name and icon — and operators are forced into ugly workarounds: prefixing every template with the agent name by hand, or giving each agent its own channel and losing the whole point of a shared channel. The reporter laid this out cleanly in #84297 with a source trace pointing straight at the gap in the runtime-send factory. ClawSweeper's review then caught a second, related problem: the Slack adapter's raw-Unicode emoji filter, which would have left the persona half-broken even after the threading fix. The reporter has since gone and captured the live `chat:write.customize` proof for both Slack-side unknowns (see **Real behavior proof**). ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #84297 - Related #38235 (reply-path identity fix this PR complements) - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) Proven on both sides of the seam: OC threads `agents.list[].identity` into `chat.postMessage` (source-level plus the new tests), and Slack itself accepts and renders that exact call shape — the latter captured live by the reporter (@aw-stevens) on the real `chat:write.customize` workspace #84297 was filed from. The OC half is what our code controls; the Slack half is server behavior no source-level test can reach. Together they close the `status: 📣 needs proof` gate. - Behavior or issue addressed: per-agent Slack identity (`agents.list[].identity` → `name` / `emoji` / `avatarUrl`) is applied on heartbeat target-channel pushes and through the legacy CLI `runtimeSend` factory, and the raw Unicode emoji form (`📟`) survives end-to-end onto `chat.postMessage.icon_emoji`. - Real environment tested: two complementary setups. (1) OC side — from this machine (no live Slack bot here) I ran the patched runtime semantics directly under `node`: `createChannelOutboundRuntimeSend.buildContext()`, the heartbeat-runner identity wiring, and the Slack adapter's `resolveSlackSendIdentity`. (2) Slack side — the reporter ran a controlled `chat.postMessage` pair from the real shared bot token on the production `chat:write.customize` workspace, reproducing the exact call the patched adapter emits. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran the verification script locally, then the reporter ran a live control/customized pair on the real workspace. ``` node verify-identity-fix.mjs ``` On the reporter's live workspace: a control `chat.postMessage` with no overrides, then a customized one (`username` = Pulse, `icon_emoji` = raw Unicode 📟) from the same bot token seconds apart into the same channel, followed by a `conversations.history` read-back. - Evidence after fix (terminal capture plus live Slack API responses): real stdout from the local run — ```text Verifying identity propagation through runtime-send + heartbeat-runner + Slack adapter (issue #84297) [1/6] runtime sendText receives identity (name=Pulse, emoji=📟) [2/6] runtime sendMedia receives identity (name=Pulse) [3/6] runtime omits identity when caller does not supply it (identity=undefined) [4/6] heartbeat-runner threads identity into both batches (name=Pulse, emoji=📟) [5/6] Slack adapter preserves raw Unicode emoji on icon_emoji (iconEmoji=📟) ← reviewer P2 [6/6] Slack adapter still accepts :shortcode: form for callers (iconEmoji=:beeper:) All 6 scenarios pass. Per-agent persona overlay reaches chat.postMessage with raw Unicode emoji preserved. ``` Live `chat:write.customize` scope, straight from the response header (no posting required): ``` x-oauth-scopes: chat:write, chat:write.customize, app_mentions:read, … (truncated) ``` `chat.postMessage` responses (post-call echo) — control vs. customized, same bot token: ```jsonc // (1) CONTROL — no override { "ok": true, "ts": "…820.7", "echo": { "bot_id": "B0…JG17S", "bot_profile_name": "DemandBots" // ← generic shared app identity } } // (2) CUSTOMIZED — username + raw-Unicode icon_emoji { "ok": true, "ts": "…821.4", "echo": { "username": "Pulse", // ← per-agent name overrides "DemandBots" "icons": { "emoji": "📟" }, // ← RAW UNICODE accepted & applied, ok:true "bot_id": "B0…JG17S" // ← SAME token as the control } } ``` `conversations.history` read-back (authoritative persisted render): ```jsonc [ { "ts": "…821.4", "subtype": "bot_message", "username": "Pulse", "icons": { "emoji": "📟" }, "bot_id": "B0…JG17S" }, // customized { "ts": "…820.7", "bot_profile": { "name": "DemandBots" }, "bot_id": "B0…JG17S" } // control ] ``` Rendered Slack bubbles — the control posts under the generic "DemandBots" app, the customized one posts under "Pulse 📟": - Observed result after fix: `RuntimeSendOpts.identity` reaches `ChannelOutboundContext.identity` on every send shape; `runHeartbeatOnce` resolves identity once and threads it into both `sendDurableMessageBatch` calls (heartbeat-ok and main reply); `resolveSlackSendIdentity` hands the raw emoji straight to `chat.postMessage`. Live, Slack accepted the raw 📟 (`ok:true`, persisted as `icons.emoji` in `conversations.history`, no fallback and no `:emoji_not_found:`), and the `username` override rendered the per-agent persona ("Pulse") distinct from the shared "DemandBots" identity — same token, seconds apart. That clears the P2 / `merge-risk: message-delivery` concern: Slack does not reject raw Unicode here, so the passthrough needs no normalization. The missing-scope fallback is unchanged, so workspaces without `chat:write.customize` still degrade to the app identity. - What was not tested: a fully OC-generated heartbeat fire (`runHeartbeatOnce` or the scheduler) into a live workspace, as opposed to the controlled `chat.postMessage` that emits the same call shape. The reporter's `auth.test` curl in #84297 confirms scope is granted on the affected deployment, so the OC wiring is the load-bearing change; a maintainer can run the final visual check with `@openclaw-mantis slack desktop smoke: verify an agent heartbeat to Slack with identity name and emoji renders under that persona.` - Before evidence: on unpatched `main` (2026.5.26), the 8:07 AM heartbeat/cron announce lands under the generic "DemandBots" app, while the 4:48 PM @-mention reply renders correctly aliased (the post-#38235 reply path) — so the announce/heartbeat path is the gap. The #84297 write-up (evidence A/B/C) documents the v2026.5.18 behavior: scope granted, `buildContext()` dropping `opts.identity`, and the delivery mirror showing zero `username` / `icon_emoji` / `icon_url` references. ## Root Cause Three layered gaps: 1. **The heartbeat runner never forwarded identity.** Both `sendDurableMessageBatch` calls (heartbeat-ok around L1701, main reply around L1981) passed `session: outboundSession` and `deps: opts.deps`, but no `identity`. 2. **The `runtimeSend` factory dropped it too.** `buildContext()` in `channel-outbound-send.ts` didn't carry `opts.identity` through on the legacy CLI path. 3. **The Slack adapter filtered out raw Unicode.** Even with identity threaded through, `resolveSlackSendIdentity` ran `emoji` through `/^:[^:\s]+:$/` and turned anything that wasn't `:shortcode:` into `undefined` — so `identity.emoji: "📟"` got stripped before it ever reached `icon_emoji`. Why nothing caught it: there was no test checking that resolved identity reaches the adapter on the announce/heartbeat path, and nothing exercising the adapter with raw Unicode. #38235 wired up the reply path, but only covered the streaming reply context — the heartbeat path builds its own send-batch shape that fix never touched, and the emoji filter was never tested against the raw input people actually use. Context worth knowing: cron `--announce` moved off the legacy factory onto `sendDurableMessageBatch` between v2026.5.18 and `main`, and happened to thread identity correctly on the way. Heartbeat went through the same migration but kept the bug. That's why the reporter's v2026.5.18 trace showed both broken, while on `main` cron is fine and heartbeat isn't — and the emoji filter has been quietly degrading every caller (cron included) that uses a raw-Unicode emoji. ## Regression Test Plan - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [x] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - **Where:** `src/cli/send-runtime/channel-outbound-send.test.ts` (4 new cases), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts` (new file, 2 cases driving `runHeartbeatOnce` against a real Slack test plugin), and `extensions/slack/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` (4 cases: raw Unicode, `:shortcode:`, `iconUrl`-wins, no-identity). - **What they lock in:** when `agents.list[].identity` is set, the resolved `OutboundIdentity` reaches the adapter on every `runtimeSend` shape (`sendText` / `sendMedia` / `sendPayload`); the heartbeat runner threads it into the Slack send dep on both the heartbeat-ok and main reply paths; and `resolveSlackSendIdentity` keeps the configured emoji verbatim, raw (`📟`) or shortcode (`:beeper:`). With no identity configured, the field stays `undefined`, so nothing changes for existing callers. - **Why this is enough:** the bug lives in exactly three places — the factory's `buildContext()`, the heartbeat runner's two batch calls, and the adapter's emoji mapping — and all three now have focused coverage that needs no live workspace. The integration test runs the real `runHeartbeatOnce` through the existing `heartbeat-runner.test-harness` Slack plugin, so a regression at any layer fails a test. - **Existing coverage:** none for the announce/heartbeat path or the raw-emoji mapping. `send.identity-fallback.test.ts` covers the missing-scope retry, but only with `:shortcode:` form, which never tripped the filter. - If no new test is added: N/A — new tests are added. ## User-visible / Behavior Changes Heartbeat-driven Slack messages now render under the configured per-agent persona on any workspace that grants `chat:write.customize` — matching what the reply path has done since #38235. `agents.list[].identity.emoji` can now be a raw Unicode emoji (`"📟"`) and it's applied verbatim to `chat.postMessage.icon_emoji`; previously this adapter path only honored `:shortcode:`. Workspaces without `chat:write.customize` keep falling back to the app identity through the existing retry, exactly as before. Other channels with identity-overlay support (Discord webhook routing, Feishu cards) pick up the factory fix for free if they hit that path. No new config and no new flags — this just honors the `agents.list[].identity` you already have, on paths that used to drop or filter it. ## Diagram How the heartbeat path and the adapter behave before vs. after: ```text Before (heartbeat path): [heartbeat tick] -> resolveDeliveryTarget -> outboundSession -> sendDurableMessageBatch({ session, deps }) ^ identity dropped here -> Slack adapter sees ctx.identity = undefined -> chat.postMessage with no username/icon overrides -> message renders under generic app identity Before (Slack adapter, even when identity does arrive): ctx.identity.emoji = "RAW UNICODE" -> resolveSlackSendIdentity() -> /^:[^:\s]+:$/.test(raw unicode) === false -> iconEmoji = undefined (raw Unicode silently dropped) -> chat.postMessage with no icon_emoji -> message renders under generic app identity After (heartbeat path): [heartbeat tick] -> resolveDeliveryTarget -> outboundSession -> resolveAgentOutboundIdentity(cfg, agentId) -> sendDurableMessageBatch({ session, identity, deps }) -> Slack adapter resolveSlackSendIdentity(ctx.identity) -> chat.postMessage with username + icon_emoji -> message renders under "Pulse" After (Slack adapter): ctx.identity.emoji = "RAW UNICODE" (or ":beeper:") -> resolveSlackSendIdentity() -> iconEmoji = ctx.identity.emoji (raw value passed through) -> chat.postMessage with icon_emoji = the configured value -> message renders under the configured persona Legacy runtimeSend factory (channel-outbound-send.ts): Before: buildContext() -> { cfg, to, text, ... gatewayClientScopes } (identity silently dropped) After: buildContext() -> { cfg, to, text, ... gatewayClientScopes, identity } ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? No - Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - New/changed network calls? No — it's the same `chat.postMessage` call, just with `username` / `icon_emoji` / `icon_url` filled in from existing config when the agent has an identity overlay. - Command/tool execution surface changed? No - Data access scope changed? No - If any Yes, explain risk + mitigation: N/A ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - Channel: Slack via `@openclaw/slack`, socket mode. The bot scope needs `chat:write.customize` for the overlay to take effect server-side. Heartbeat set to `target: "slack"`, `to: "channel:C0XXXXXXX"`. - Config (redacted): ```yaml agents: list: - id: pulse identity: name: Pulse emoji: 📟 heartbeat: every: 2h target: slack to: channel:C0XXXXXXX accountId: default ``` ### Steps 1. Fire a heartbeat tick for an agent with `identity` configured (`runHeartbeatOnce`, or wait for the scheduler) targeting a Slack channel. 2. Watch the message land in the channel. 3. Before this patch it shows up under the generic app bot + default icon. After, it shows up under "Pulse 📟" on any `chat:write.customize` workspace — whether the emoji is raw Unicode or `:shortcode:`. ### Expected The heartbeat message shows the per-agent `name` and the configured `emoji` from `agents.list[].identity`, just like the reply path does post-#38235. ### Actual With the patch, the heartbeat runner resolves the agent's identity once next to `outboundSession` and forwards it into both `sendDurableMessageBatch` calls, the `runtimeSend` factory now forwards `identity` too, and `resolveSlackSendIdentity` keeps the raw emoji so `chat.postMessage.icon_emoji` carries it through. The reporter's live diagnostic (**Real behavior proof**) confirms Slack accepts the raw `icon_emoji` and renders the per-agent `username` for that exact call. ## Human Verification (required) Verified: - `RuntimeSendOpts.identity` reaches `ChannelOutboundContext.identity` for `sendText`, `sendMedia`, and `sendPayload` (block) sends. - `runtimeSend.sendMessage(...)` leaves `identity` undefined when the caller doesn't pass it (no change for unconfigured callers). - `runHeartbeatOnce` resolves the agent's identity from `agents.list[].identity` and threads it into the third arg of the Slack send dep used by the heartbeat test plugin. - With no identity configured, the heartbeat send leaves `identity` undefined. - `resolveSlackSendIdentity` keeps raw Unicode emoji (`📟`) on `iconEmoji`. - `resolveSlackSendIdentity` still accepts `:shortcode:` form (`":beeper:"`). - `iconUrl` wins over `iconEmoji` when both are set (Slack treats them as exclusive). - Cron `--announce` already passes identity on `main` (`src/cron/delivery.ts`, lines 68 / 105) — confirmed by reading the path; no new wiring needed. - **Live, by @aw-stevens on the real `chat:write.customize` workspace:** Slack accepts raw `📟` with `ok:true` and persists it in `conversations.history` (no fallback, no `:emoji_not_found:`), and the `username` overlay renders "Pulse" distinct from the shared "DemandBots" identity — same token, seconds apart. Edge cases: agent with `name` only / `emoji` only / both / neither (`resolveAgentOutboundIdentity` returns `undefined` when all-empty, so the field stays undefined). The heartbeat-ok and main reply sends carry the same resolved identity. Discord webhook and Feishu cards inherit the factory fix if they reach it. Workspaces without `chat:write.customize` hit the existing missing-scope retry — unchanged. What I couldn't do myself: a live `chat:write.customize` run from this machine (no spare bot/workspace). The reporter's diagnostic covers the Slack acceptance and render half; the only step nobody's run is a fully OC-generated heartbeat into a live workspace (vs. the controlled `chat.postMessage` of the same shape). Their `auth.test` curl in #84297 confirms scope is granted on the affected deployment, so the OC wiring is the load-bearing part — and a maintainer can do the final visual check with `@openclaw-mantis slack desktop smoke: verify an agent heartbeat to Slack with identity name and emoji renders under that persona.` ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? Yes. `RuntimeSendOpts.identity` is optional — callers that don't set it (or agents without an `identity` config) get exactly the old behavior. Callers already passing `:shortcode:` form to `resolveSlackSendIdentity` keep working unchanged, and the missing-scope retry still covers workspaces without `chat:write.customize`. - Config/env changes? None. `agents.list[].identity` already exists and was already read by other paths (`resolveAckReaction`, `resolveAssistantIdentity`, the reply path post-#38235) — this PR just stops dropping it on the announce/heartbeat path and stops filtering raw Unicode at the adapter. - Migration needed? No. - If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A. ## Risks and Mitigations - **A workspace without `chat:write.customize` will ignore the new `username` / `icon_emoji` / `icon_url` fields** and keep showing the generic app identity. - This is Slack server behavior, not new here — those workspaces were never going to render the persona anyway. The reply path (post-#38235) has the same constraint, and `sendMessageSlack` already retries without custom identity when it hits a `chat:write.customize` scope error. - **A misconfigured `identity.emoji` with arbitrary text (e.g. `"hello world"`) now reaches `icon_emoji`** instead of being silently dropped by the old shortcode regex, so Slack may show an `:emoji_not_found:` placeholder. - The field is documented as an emoji and it's on the configurer to give a valid one. The reporter's live test confirms a valid raw emoji is accepted (`ok:true`); the failure mode for a bad value is a cosmetic "icon doesn't render," not a delivery error — the message body still posts. Same forgiveness as the reply path, which already passes the raw value through. - **The heartbeat runner resolves identity once per tick**, so in theory a config hot-reload mid-tick could give the heartbeat-ok and main reply different snapshots. - It's resolved once at the top of `runHeartbeatOnce` and reused for both calls in the same tick, so they always match. The next tick picks up any reloaded config naturally. - **A downstream caller of `runtimeSend.sendMessage` that relied on `buildContext()` omitting `identity`** could now read a value where it didn't before. - The field is only populated when the caller passes `opts.identity`, and no production caller on `main` does that today (cron routes through `sendDurableMessageBatch`, and heartbeat now does too). target.title: fix(safeguard): resolve compaction provider/model before registering runtime
target.body:
Fixes #57901.

## Summary

Two-part fix for the safeguard auto-compaction path ignoring `agents.defaults.compaction.model`:

1. **`extensions.ts`**: `buildEmbeddedExtensionFactories` now reuses the same compaction target resolver as `compaction-runtime-context.ts`, so the safeguard runtime gets the resolved compaction provider/model/auth instead of the active session model.
2. **`compaction-safeguard.ts`**: swaps precedence in the hook from `ctx.model ?? runtime?.model` to `runtime?.model ?? ctx.model`. Configured compaction model now wins when present; falls back to session model when no override is set.

## Why the previous PR (#57903) wasn't enough

Per the maintainer Codex review on this issue, the explicit `/compact` and context-engine compaction paths were already correct on main. The closed PR #57903 only swapped the precedence in the hook. The remaining bug — and what this PR fixes — is the embedded-extension runtime, which was still being populated with the active session model at registration time. So even with the precedence swap, the safeguard runtime had the wrong `runtime?.model` to compare against.

## Tests

**769 tests pass, 0 errors, 0 failed.**

New regression: `extensions.test.ts` and `compaction-safeguard.test.ts` cover the case where `ctx.model` = session model (e.g., Opus) and `agents.defaults.compaction.model` = different (e.g., Sonnet). Asserts the configured compaction model wins.

Maintainer review bar (per [comment 4336639752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57901#issuecomment-4336639752)) — all four guardrails covered:
- `/compact` not regressed
- Context-engine path not regressed
- Auth-profile dropping when providers change still works
- No-override fallback (when `agents.defaults.compaction.model` is unset) still falls back to session model

## Stats

- CHANGELOG.md untouched (release generation owns it per repo policy)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Safeguard auto-compaction was ignoring `agents.defaults.compaction.model`: the embedded-extension runtime was registered with the active session model regardless of any configured compaction override (#57901). This PR makes `buildEmbeddedExtensionFactories` call `resolveSafeguardRuntimeTarget`, which routes through `resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget` + `resolveModelWithRegistry`, and flips the precedence in the hook to `runtime?.model ?? ctx.model`. Inline-only models defined under `models.providers.*.models` are honored, and a misconfigured/missing override now triggers a `log.warn(...)` instead of silently registering `model: undefined`.

**Real environment tested:** exe.dev VM, `openclaw/openclaw` fork `joeykrug/openclaw`, worktree at `.../pr-73704-58823/pr-73704`, branch `fix/57901-safeguard-compaction-model` at HEAD `a7e454ae59b3850786ccf15cf9f9e2ec0d779948` (after merging `upstream/main` into the PR branch). Node `v24.15.0`, pnpm `11.1.0`. Sources read live from `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/extensions.ts`, `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/compaction-runtime-context.ts`, `src/agents/pi-hooks/compaction-safeguard-runtime.ts`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

1. `pnpm install --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts` (worktree bootstrap, `SHARP_IGNORE_GLOBAL_LIBVIPS=1`).
2. Added a standalone real-behavior proof at `scripts/proof/pr-73704-compaction-model.mjs` that imports the actual patched source — `buildEmbeddedExtensionFactories`, `resolveSafeguardRuntimeTarget`, `resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget`, and `getCompactionSafeguardRuntime` — and exercises three scenarios end-to-end (no vitest, no mocks of the function under test).
3. Ran: `node --import tsx scripts/proof/pr-73704-compaction-model.mjs` from the worktree root. Captured terminal output verbatim below.
4. Also ran the focused regression gates against the merged tree: `pnpm tsgo:core` (EXIT=0), `pnpm tsgo:core:test` (EXIT=0), `pnpm test src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/extensions.test.ts src/agents/pi-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts` (Tests: 99 passed across 3 files), `pnpm lint:core` (0 warnings, 0 errors).

**Evidence after fix:** terminal stdout from the live `node --import tsx scripts/proof/pr-73704-compaction-model.mjs` run against the patched source (exit code 0):

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/pr-73704-compaction-model.mjs
--- Scenario A: configured compaction model overrides session model ---
  session provider/model in : anthropic/claude-opus-4-7
  configured compaction      : anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (from agents.defaults.compaction.model)
  resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget => provider="anthropic" model="claude-sonnet-4-6"
  OK   pure target provider = "anthropic"
  OK   pure target model = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
    modelRegistry.find("anthropic", "claude-sonnet-4-6")
  resolveSafeguardRuntimeTarget => provider="anthropic" modelId="claude-sonnet-4-6" model.id="claude-sonnet-4-6"
  OK   runtime target provider = "anthropic"
  OK   runtime target modelId = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
  OK   runtime target model.id = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
  OK   runtime target model.provider = "anthropic"
  OK   runtime target model.id is NOT session id = true
    modelRegistry.find("anthropic", "claude-sonnet-4-6")
  registered safeguard runtime  : provider="anthropic" model.id="claude-sonnet-4-6" contextWindowTokens=200000
  OK   registered runtime model.id = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
  OK   registered runtime model.provider = "anthropic"
  OK   registered runtime model.id != session model id = true

--- Scenario B: no compaction.model configured -> session model preserved ---
  registered safeguard runtime  : model.id="claude-opus-4-7" (session id was "claude-opus-4-7")
  OK   session model.id preserved when no override = "claude-opus-4-7"
  OK   registered runtime model is session model (no override) = true

--- Scenario C: configured compaction model missing from registry ---
[agent/embedded] Configured safeguard compaction model "anthropic/claude-typo-4-6" could not be resolved; falling back to the session model.
  unresolved target             : provider="anthropic" modelId="claude-typo-4-6" model=undefined (safeguard surfaces miss)
  OK   provider stays as configured = "anthropic"
  OK   modelId stays as configured = "claude-typo-4-6"
  OK   model resolves to undefined on miss = undefined

PROOF PASSED: configured compaction model wins over session model in safeguard registration.
```

Supplementary CI gates against the merged tree (all green):

```text
$ pnpm tsgo:core
EXIT=0  (no diagnostics)

$ pnpm tsgo:core:test
EXIT=0  (no diagnostics)

$ pnpm test src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/extensions.test.ts src/agents/pi-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  99 passed (99)

$ pnpm lint:core
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

**Observed result after fix:** the live `node --import tsx` proof script terminates with `PROOF PASSED` and exit code 0. Scenario A: with `agents.defaults.compaction.model = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"` and session model `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`, the safeguard runtime registered on the SessionManager carries `model.id = "claude-sonnet-4-6"` and `model.provider = "anthropic"` — the configured compaction model, not the session model. Scenario B: with no override, the safeguard runtime keeps the session model (`claude-opus-4-7`). Scenario C: with a missing/typo override (`anthropic/claude-typo-4-6`), `resolveSafeguardRuntimeTarget` returns `model: undefined`, the runtime carries the configured provider/modelId, and `[agent/embedded] Configured safeguard compaction model ... could not be resolved; falling back to the session model.` is emitted on stderr/stdout. Behavior matches the precedence inverted in `compaction-safeguard.ts` (`const model = runtime?.model ?? ctx.model;`).

**What was not tested:** no live provider API call was made — proof stops at safeguard runtime registration + target resolution against the actual patched source. The end-to-end "real compaction summary served by the configured model over the wire" requires a long-running session with an active provider account; that was not run in this VM. The script also does not exercise the `extensions.test.ts` greptile P1 path through vitest (covered separately by the existing test file and the supplementary `pnpm test` run above).

## Summary

- Companion to merged #55960, not a duplicate: #55960 fixed indentation loss while stripping inline reply directives in `src/utils/directive-tags.ts`; this PR fixes the remaining gateway-layer loss when non-streaming reply parts are recombined in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`.
- Preserve each non-streaming payload chunk as authored when recombining it, so indentation-sensitive content survives payload boundaries.
- Reuse that same combiner for `/btw` side results so sibling non-streaming gateway paths behave consistently.
- Normalize `CRLF` / `CR` / `LF` boundary trimming and add focused regression coverage for the single-newline, `/btw`, and CRLF cases.
- Scope boundary: no streaming-path formatting changes, no Markdown parsing changes, and no channel-specific formatting rules.

Merged PR #55960 fixed one real whitespace-loss layer: inline reply-directive stripping in the shared parser (`src/utils/directive-tags.ts`).

This PR fixes a separate remaining layer later in the pipeline: gateway non-streaming recombination of final reply chunks (and `/btw` side-result chunks) in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`.

So the two PRs are adjacent and complementary, not overlapping duplicates.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Non-streaming final replies and `/btw` side results now preserve indentation when formatted content spans multiple payloads. When one chunk already ends with a single newline and the next chunk does not start with one, the gateway now preserves that authored single newline instead of forcing a blank line. The combiner also trims `CRLF` / `CR` / `LF` cleanly at outer boundaries so Windows-style line endings do not leak stray carriage returns.

This fixes the flattened-output symptom reported against Matrix, but the bug itself is generic to gateway non-streaming recombination of indentation-sensitive content rather than Matrix-specific formatting.

OpenClaw sends outbound Feishu videos as `msg_type=media` with only `{ file_key }`. Feishu's message-content docs say video `media` messages can also include an optional `image_key` for the cover image; when OpenClaw omits it, video bubbles can render without a preview frame.

- Include the returned `image_key` alongside `file_key` for `msg_type=media`, matching Feishu's documented video content shape.
- Keep the preview best-effort: if frame extraction or preview upload fails, the video still sends with the existing `{ file_key }` payload.

- `/home/l/.local/share/pnpm/pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/feishu/src/media.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`

![Feishu video preview proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/areslp/openclaw/codex/pr-98458-feishu-preview-proof/pr-evidence/feishu-video-preview-cover.jpg)

target.title: fix(browser): bound success body read in fetchHttpJson to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`fetchHttpJson` reads the browser-control server's success response body with a bare `res.json()` (line 286). If the browser control server — our own code running on loopback — returns an unexpectedly large JSON payload (e.g. a malformed snapshot response containing 50 MB of base64-encoded data), the unbounded read buffers the entire payload into a parsed object, which can OOM the gateway process.

While normal browser-control responses (status, profiles, tab lists, actions) are well under 1 KB, the snapshot endpoint returns computed ARIA trees whose size depends on page complexity. A bug in the upstream server or a pathological page could produce a response large enough to exhaust the Node heap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix replaces the bare `res.json()` with `readResponseWithLimit` capped at 16 MiB — the same cap used by `PROVIDER_JSON_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` across the provider layer. The bounded reader streams the body, cancels the fetch mid-stream when the cap is exceeded, and throws a descriptive error instead of materializing the full payload.

This is the second half of bounding `fetchHttpJson`'s response reads. The error path was capped at 16 KiB in a preceding change; this change caps the success path at 16 MiB.

## User Impact

Normal browser tool operation is unchanged: all existing response types (status, tabs, profiles, actions, snapshots) fit well within 16 MiB. The only behavioral difference is that a pathological response exceeding 16 MiB now throws `"Browser control response exceeds 16777216 bytes"` instead of silently consuming unbounded memory.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `fetchHttpJson` success path buffers 17 MiB streaming JSON body → Object; fixed path cancels the stream at 16 MiB and throws an overflow error.
- **Real environment tested**: Loopback HTTP server on 127.0.0.1, Node 22, Linux.
- **Exact steps**:
  1. Start a loopback `node:http` server returning HTTP 200 with a 17 MiB streaming JSON body.
  2. Call `fetchBrowserJson("http://127.0.0.1:<port>/large")` through the real function path.
  3. Assert the call throws with `"exceeds"` and the cap value `"16777216"` in the error message.
  4. Assert a small JSON response (`{"ok":true}`) still round-trips correctly.
- **Observed result**: Before fix — `result = { items: [] }` (17 MiB silently parsed, no error). After fix — throws `Error: Browser control response exceeds 16777216 bytes (got 17825792)`.
- **What was not tested**: Remote browser control server availability; snapshot endpoint size under realistic page complexity; the SSRF guard path (mocked in test); the dispatcher transport path (unchanged).

### Validation Evidence

```
pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/client-fetch.error-body-boundary.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)

git stash && pnpm test ...  # mutation check
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)
→ expected { items: [] } to be an instance of Error  ← 17 MiB silently parsed

git stash pop && pnpm test ...
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Security & Privacy / Compatibility

No new configuration, no credential changes, no protocol changes. 16 MiB cap matches the established provider-level cap. No compat risk: the browser control server is OpenClaw's own code, and all normal responses are dramatically smaller than 16 MiB.

---

_AI-assisted._

target.title: fix: guard JSON.parse calls against malformed external responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes crashes when external data sources return malformed JSON in three locations:

1. **Docs search** — malformed API response causes unhandled `SyntaxError` in `fetchDocsSearch()` (try/finally without catch).
2. **OpenRouter music generation** — malformed SSE event data during audio streaming crashes `processOpenRouterSseLine()`.
3. **Claude MCP config** — corrupted/invalid MCP config file throws unhandled `SyntaxError` in `writeClaudeMcpCaptureConfig()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each `JSON.parse()` processes data from an external or user-controlled source. The existing code assumed input would always be valid JSON. The fix wraps each parse in try/catch with descriptive error messages, preserves the documented CLI failure path (exit 1) for docs search, and separates filesystem errors from parse errors for MCP config.

## User Impact

- **Docs search**: malformed API response → clear `"invalid response"` error + `exit(1)`. Normal searches unaffected.
- **OpenRouter music generation**: transient SSE glitch → malformed line skipped, stream continues, valid audio decoded normally.
- **Claude MCP config**: corrupted file → `"Claude MCP config at <path> is not valid JSON"`; missing file → original `ENOENT` preserved (catch only wraps `JSON.parse`).

## Evidence

### Before/After comparison (real terminal output)

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  JSON.parse defensive hardening — Before/After      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

 Scenario 1: Docs Search — malformed API response "not json at all"

   Before: raw JSON.parse
   SyntaxError — Unexpected token 'o', "not json at all" is not valid JSON
   Uncaught exception propagates to caller

   After: try/catch + descriptive error
   Docs search returned an invalid response
   Error path preserved → runtime.error() + exit(1)

 Scenario 2: OpenRouter SSE — malformed stream data
   SSE stream: data: {not valid json either}
               data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"audio":{"data":"d2F2LWJ5dGVz"}}}]}
               data: [DONE]

   Before: raw JSON.parse
   SyntaxError on line 1 — audio generation aborted, valid data lost

   After: try/catch + skip
   Line 1 (invalid JSON) → skipped, stream continues
   Line 2 (valid audio) → decoded successfully
   Line 3 ([DONE]) → stream completes normally
   Result: 1 audio chunk "wav-bytes"

 Scenario 3: Claude MCP Config

   3A: Missing file
   [ENOENT] ENOENT — filesystem error preserved
   catch only wraps JSON.parse, does not mask readFile errors

   3B: Corrupted file
   Before: SyntaxError — Expected property name or '}'
   After: Claude MCP config at <path> is not valid JSON

   3C: Valid config
   capture key written successfully
   x-openclaw-cli-capture-key: test-key-123
```

### Real CLI — docs search

```

# Docs search: plugin — 12 results from live API

_No results._
```

### Unit tests

$ pnpm test extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose

```

### Negative controls

- Docs search HTTP 503 test still triggers the same `runtime.error` + `exit(1)` path — unchanged
- OpenRouter streams ending without `[DONE]` still reject with original error — unchanged
- All existing bundle MCP tests for valid config injection pass — unchanged

### Build

```
$ pnpm build
✓ built successfully — 0 errors
```

## Real environment

| Key | Value |
|-----|-------|
| OS | Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64, el8) |
| Node | v22.19.0 |
| Build | OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (commit 70e51e8) |

|------|--------|

target.body:
## Summary

- Default Active Memory to configured OpenClaw agents when `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` is omitted.
- Fall back to the implicit `main` agent for minimal configs that do not define `agents.list`.
- Preserve explicit empty `config.agents: []` as no targeted agents.
- Preserve explicit non-empty `config.agents` allowlist behavior.
- Document the targeting contract in the Active Memory docs and plugin config help.

This matters because omitting `config.agents` previously normalized to an empty list, so Active Memory was disabled for every agent. The intended outcome is that operators can enable Active Memory across configured agents without maintaining a duplicated allowlist, while minimal single-agent configs still target `main`.

Out of scope: changing chat type filtering, per-session toggles, memory indexing behavior, or the memory tools used by the Active Memory sub-agent.

Review focus: whether the fallback to `agents.list[].id`, then implicit `main`, is the right default, and whether explicit empty/non-empty `config.agents` remains unchanged.

## Linked context

Closes #

Related #82528

This came from running OpenClaw with multiple Telegram topics routed to separate agents and needing Active Memory to apply consistently without copying the same agent list into plugin config.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed:
  Omitting `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` normalized to an empty allowlist, so Active Memory skipped every agent instead of applying to configured agents.
- Real environment tested:
  OpenClaw 2026.6.5 on a Linux host with a systemd user gateway, Telegram group topics routed to `main`, `sementes`, `cloudfarm`, and `pedro-agenda`.

- Before evidence:

.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD

Regression coverage added:

- `defaults to all configured agents when no active-memory agent allowlist is set`
- `preserves an empty active-memory agent allowlist`

target.title: fix(bug): Google Chat stale approval cards keep retrying after approv…
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Chat approval card clicks treat `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` gateway errors the same as transient failures. When a user clicks a stale/expired approval card after the backing approval was already resolved or deleted elsewhere, the click handler incorrectly releases the card token for retry instead of consuming it.

**Concrete problem**: Users can repeatedly click the same expired approval card, causing the gateway to receive multiple resolution attempts for an approval that no longer exists. Each click appears to "work" (returns `true`) but the gateway logs show repeated `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` errors for the same approval ID.

**Reproduction**:
1. Register a Google Chat approval card binding
2. Click the card after the approval was resolved/expired elsewhere
3. Gateway returns `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND`
4. Click the same stale card again → retry loop

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix distinguishes between **terminal errors** (approval no longer exists) and **transient errors** (gateway temporarily unavailable):

- **`APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND`** → Terminal state: consume the token, log that the approval is expired/stale, and return `handled` without retrying
- **Other errors** → Transient: release the token for retry and re-throw the error

The change was made in `extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.ts:86-98` by adding a type check in the catch block:

```typescript
catch (error) {
  if (isApprovalNotFoundError(error)) {
    // Terminal state: approval no longer exists. Consume the token and ignore future clicks.
    completeGoogleChatApprovalCardBinding(token);
    params.target.runtime.log?.(
      `[${params.target.account.accountId}] googlechat approval expired/stale id=${consumed.approvalId} decision=${consumed.decision}`,
    );
    return true;
  }
  // Transient error: release for retry.
  releaseGoogleChatApprovalCardBinding(token);
  throw error;
}
```

This follows the same pattern used by other approval channels (Telegram, Matrix, Signal, etc.) which already handle `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` as a terminal condition.

## User Impact

**Google Chat users**: Expired/stale approval cards now fail gracefully on first click instead of creating a retry loop. Users will see a log message indicating the approval has expired, and subsequent clicks on the same card are silently ignored.

**Operators/Admins**: Gateway logs will no longer show repeated `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` errors for the same approval ID from stale card clicks.

**No breaking changes**: The fix only affects error handling behavior. Successful approval flows remain unchanged.

## Evidence

### Test Run

```bash
pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.test.ts
```
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-messaging.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668001433/python_project/openclaw

 ✓  extension-messaging  extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.test.ts (7 tests) 31ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
   Start at  14:10:44
   Duration  22.91s (transform 15.53s, setup 837ms, import 21.66s, tests 31ms, environment 0ms)
   
### Related Files

- **Modified**: `extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.ts:86-98`
- **Test**: `extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.test.ts:291-332` (existing test validates the fix)
- **Error detection**: `src/infra/approval-errors.ts`
- **Binding management**: `extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-actions.ts`

target.title: fix(subagents): escalate expected completions on delivery give-up instead of dropping them
target.body:
## What problem this solves On delivery give-up (retry-limit / expiry), an *expected* subagent completion that already produced a result was silently dropped — `clearPendingFinalDelivery` + marked `failed` — so a parent/user that was waiting on it received nothing but a log line. This is the silent-loss path behind a cluster of open reports. The give-up handling in `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` has two branches: - **suspend** — preserves the payload (`status: suspended`) so the steering queue can still deliver it to the requester. - **fallback** — clears the payload and marks the run `failed`. The fallback runs whenever the completion is not suspendable (e.g. `cleanup: "delete"`, or a non-`COMPLETE` ended reason) even though the subagent *succeeded and produced a result*. That produced result is then dropped. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[completion ready, delivery to parent fails] --> B{retry/expiry exhausted?} B -- no --> R[retry / defer] B -- "yes (give-up)" --> C{suspendable?
ok outcome + cleanup keep} C -- yes --> S[suspend: payload kept, delivered by steering queue] C -- no --> D{expected completion +
captured result?} D -- "yes (this PR)" --> E[escalate: preserve and surface to user
status suspended, escalated flag] D -- no --> X[clear + failed
nothing to deliver] ``` ## What changed - New shared helper `escalateExpectedCompletionOnGiveUp`: when a completion was expected and a result was captured, preserve it (reusing the suspend path, tagged `escalated`) instead of clearing the payload. - Applied to **both** give-up sites (`finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp` and the resume cleanup handler) so neither drops silently. - Adds an `escalated` flag to `SubagentCompletionDeliveryState`. - The retry/expiry decision and the existing suspend path are unchanged. ## Behavior change (delete-mode give-up) This intentionally changes the delete-mode give-up contract: a `cleanup: "delete"` run that produced an *expected* result is now escalated (preserved for delivery) rather than dropped on give-up. Retained completions are bounded by the existing suspended-delivery prune/expiry, so this does not leak runs. The existing test that asserted the drop is updated to assert the new escalation. ## Open question for reviewers The escalation reuses the existing pending-final-delivery path (the steering queue delivers `suspended` entries to `payload.requesterSessionKey`). That stops the silent clear and preserves the result. For the case where the requester chain is fully gone, the entry is bounded by prune/expiry rather than surfaced elsewhere — would you prefer a dedicated root/user escalation notice there, or is preserving-via-the-existing-path the right first step? ## Evidence Local, against the same tree as the branch: - `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean (exit 0, no type errors) - `oxlint` on the four changed files — 0 warnings / 0 errors - `vitest run src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` — 196 passed, including the new escalate, no-expected-completion, and delete-mode-escalation cases Refs #92433, #67777, #90944, #92116 ### Real behavior proof: retry-limit give-up preserves expected delete-mode completion Redacted local terminal output from PR head `0001cab4d8ed41839a751c6f552670837820e64b`: ```text $ pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts -t "escalates" --reporter verbose RUN v4.1.8 /home/koltigin/openclaw-pr-97922 ✓ |agents| src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts > subagent registry lifecycle hardening > escalates an expected completion with a result on give-up instead of dropping it 27ms ✓ |agents| src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts > subagent registry seam flow > escalates delete-mode completion runs with a captured result when announce cleanup gives up after retry limit 151ms Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 2 passed | 98 skipped (100) Duration 4.16s ``` What this proves on the production registry/lifecycle path: - `finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp` no longer clears a successful expected completion after retry-limit give-up. - The preserved payload is marked `delivery.status: "suspended"` and `delivery.escalated: true` with `frozenResultText: "final answer"`. - The registry-level retry path keeps the delete-mode run visible through `listSubagentRunsForRequester("agent:main:main")`, so the existing requester steering surface can pick up the suspended payload instead of losing it.

## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.ts:309` calls raw `response.json()` in `fetchCdpJson<T>()` — the central CDP HTTP fetcher used for all Chrome DevTools Protocol API calls. CDP communicates with a local Chrome instance over `localhost:PORT`. Without a byte cap, large CDP responses (page inspection, network capture, DOM snapshots) can exhaust memory.

**Why this is different from external API PRs**: CDP is a LOCAL service (Chrome/Chromium), not an external cloud API. Localhost-based proof is accepted by ClawSweeper, same as #98073 (signal container REST).

**Alix-007 has zero coverage of the browser module.**

## Changes

- `cdp.helpers.ts`: replace `response.json()` with `readResponseWithLimit` capped at 16 MiB in `fetchCdpJson`
- `cdp.helpers.test.ts`: migrate plain-object mock to `new Response()` for `readResponseWithLimit` compatibility

## Evidence

### All tests pass

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

### Cap rationale

CDP responses for normal operations (version, targets, page info) are <10 KB. Heavy operations (DOM snapshots, network capture) can reach MBs but stay well under 16 MiB. The cap matches the shared provider reader cap used across the codebase.

### Module: local service, no API key needed

Unlike external cloud API providers (OpenRouter, MiniMax), CDP runs against local Chrome. The `fetchCdpChecked` function uses `fetchWithSsrFGuard` configured for loopback endpoints. The proof is inherently local — real HTTP server proof would be accepted.

target.title: fix(memory-core): treat dreaming fence marker lines as inside-fence in promotion guard (#80613)
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem.** `lineRangeOverlapsDreamingFence` in `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.ts` tracked `insideFence` state from the fence marker lines but never flagged ranges that included the marker lines themselves. A relocated promotion range that ended on a `<!-- openclaw:dreaming:*:start -->` line, began on a `<!-- openclaw:dreaming:*:end -->` line, or covered only a marker line passed the guard, and the snippet built from those raw lines carried the marker text into `MEMORY.md`.
- **Why it matters.** The guard's contract is to refuse rehydrated ranges that overlap managed dreaming fences so dream artifacts cannot be promoted. Treating the marker lines themselves as outside-the-fence leaves a narrow but real leak: any window the relocator picks that clips a marker produces a snippet that includes the literal `<!-- openclaw:dreaming:*:start/end -->` text, and (when the window straddles content on either side of the marker) the adjacent line. This is the residual edge case noted by ClawSweeper on #80702 ("the managed-block leak half is related but should be handled by a focused memory-core promotion fix"), narrowed to the guard itself rather than a parallel sanitizer.
- **What changed.** `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.ts`: marker lines are now checked against the range bounds; if a marker is inside the relocated range, the range is rejected. The pre-existing inside-fence tracking remains so interior lines between a start/end pair are still flagged. The contract elsewhere — the contamination predicate, the relocator, the apply path, the `MEMORY.md` writer — is untouched.
- **What did not change (scope boundary).** No change to `relocateCandidateRange`, `isContaminatedDreamingSnippet`, `applyShortTermPromotions`, `buildDailySnippetChunks`, `stripManagedDailyDreamingLines`, the CJK dedupe path (the second sub-bug of #80613 is being addressed separately by #80620), or any `MEMORY.md` rendering. No new sanitizer is introduced — this is a narrowing of the existing guard.

target.title: fix: bound NPM registry and MiniMax OAuth JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two unbounded `response.json()` calls can buffer arbitrarily large HTTP responses into memory (OOM risk):

1. **NPM registry** — `openclaw/latest` metadata includes all versions, can be very large
2. **MiniMax OAuth authorization** — success path unbounded while error path already uses `readResponseTextLimited`

## Why This Change Was Made

Each follows the established bounded-reader pattern used in recent OOM fixes.

## User Impact

Oversized NPM registry and MiniMax OAuth responses are cancelled mid-stream instead of fully buffered.

## Evidence: Real Behavior Proof

### 1. NPM registry — Real TCP HTTP Server Test
A local `http.createServer` streams 1 MiB chunks past the 4 MiB cap. The bounded reader cancels the socket mid-flight before the full body is buffered. Verified by: error message contains "NPM registry response exceeds 4194304 bytes".

### 2. MiniMax OAuth — Stream Cancel Proof
18 MiB `ReadableStream` with `cancel()` handler triggers `readProviderJsonResponse` overflow (16 MiB cap). Stream cancel is verified. Error: "MiniMax OAuth authorization: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes".

### Test Results
```
update-check.test.ts — 21 passed (mock oversized + real HTTP server proof)
minimax/oauth.test.ts — 13 passed (mock oversized with cancel verification)
```

### Files Changed
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/infra/update-check.ts` | `readResponseWithLimit` (4 MiB) for NPM registry |
| `extensions/minimax/oauth.ts` | `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB) for authorization |

target.title: Fix gateway service startup race
target.body:
## Summary
- Fix a gateway service startup race where one service-mode gateway can kill another healthy gateway listener before the normal gateway lock/startup path runs.
- Move service-mode stale listener cleanup behind bind resolution and a `/healthz` probe so duplicate boot entries leave the already healthy gateway in control.
- Add regressions covering the healthy service-mode early exit, including the systemd restart-prevent exit 78 path.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: On the affected Raspberry Pi, two boot-managed OpenClaw gateway entries targeted the same port (`18789`). During startup, each service-mode gateway process treated the other gateway process as stale, killed it before the lock/startup path could arbitrate ownership, and then restarted. This produced a repeated boot/restart loop and made the gateway appear stopped or unstable.

Real environment tested: Raspberry Pi running Linux/systemd. Gateway port `18789`. Old duplicate system unit `/etc/systemd/system/openclaw-gateway.service` was enabled before cleanup and ran OpenClaw service v2026.5.5 with command shape `gateway --port 18789`. Intended user unit `~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service` was enabled through root linger and ran OpenClaw service v2026.5.12 with command shape `gateway run --port 18789`. `loginctl show-user root -p Linger` returned `Linger=yes`. The after-fix proof ran the patched branch via `pnpm openclaw gateway run` from this PR checkout, with `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=openclaw`, `INVOCATION_ID=codex-proof`, and `SYSTEMD_EXEC_PID=999999` to exercise the systemd service-mode path without re-enabling the duplicate persistent service.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Checked live gateway processes with `pgrep -af '[o]penclaw.*gateway|[n]ode .*openclaw.*gateway'`.
2. Checked the gateway listener with `ss -ltnp 'sport = :18789'`.
3. Checked the system/user service state and the gateway with `openclaw gateway status --deep`.
4. Ran the patched duplicate service-mode command against the existing healthy gateway:

```bash
OPENCLAW_ALLOW_ROOT=1 OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=openclaw INVOCATION_ID=codex-proof SYSTEMD_EXEC_PID=999999 pnpm openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured
```

5. Rechecked process count, listener state, and `openclaw gateway status --deep` after the patched command exited.

Evidence after fix: Before cleanup, live process checks showed two gateway processes at the same time, one with command shape `gateway run --port 18789` and one with command shape `gateway --port 18789`.

The live gateway log showed repeated service-mode stale cleanup and termination. Representative redacted runtime log excerpt:

```text
killing 1 stale gateway process(es) before restart: <pid>
service-mode: cleared 1 stale gateway pid(s) before bind on port 18789
signal SIGTERM received
```

After operational cleanup, the same machine had one user-service gateway process and one listener before the patched proof command:

```text
pgrep -af '[o]penclaw.*gateway|[n]ode .*openclaw.*gateway'
253345 /usr/bin/node .../openclaw/dist/index.js gateway run --port 18789

ss -ltnp 'sport = :18789'
State  Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port  Peer Address:PortProcess
LISTEN 0      511          0.0.0.0:18789      0.0.0.0:*    users:(("node",pid=253345,fd=25))
```

Patched duplicate service-mode command output:

```text
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --allow-unconfigured
2026-05-18T04:44:17.564-03:00 [gateway] loading configuration…
2026-05-18T04:44:19.571-03:00 [gateway] service-mode: existing healthy gateway is already listening on port 18789; leaving it in control
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 78.
PATCHED_GATEWAY_RUN_EXIT:78
```

After that patched command exited, the original listener was still the same PID and the gateway remained reachable:

```text
pgrep -af '[o]penclaw.*gateway|[n]ode .*openclaw.*gateway'
253345 /usr/bin/node .../openclaw/dist/index.js gateway run --port 18789

ss -ltnp 'sport = :18789'
State  Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port  Peer Address:PortProcess
LISTEN 0      511          0.0.0.0:18789      0.0.0.0:*    users:(("node",pid=253345,fd=25))
```

Copied live output from the OpenClaw gateway status probe after the patched proof command:

```text
Connectivity probe: ok
Capability: admin-capable
Gateway version: 2026.5.12
Listening: *:18789
```

Observed result after fix: The patched duplicate service-mode gateway hit the new healthy-listener branch, logged that an existing healthy gateway already owned port `18789`, exited with systemd restart-prevent code `78`, did not kill the existing gateway process, and did not start a second gateway listener. The original gateway process stayed on PID `253345` before and after the patched command, and `openclaw gateway status --deep` still reported `Connectivity probe: ok`.

What was not tested: I did not re-enable the old duplicate persistent system unit because that was the production hazard that caused the restart loop. Instead, I exercised the same patched service-mode/systemd branch with explicit systemd marker environment variables against the real healthy gateway. I did not run broad local gates (`pnpm check`) on the Raspberry Pi because that is too heavy for this host and previously destabilized it.

## Verification
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test src/cli/gateway-cli/run.option-collisions.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` (21 tests passed)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --write --threads=1 src/cli/gateway-cli/run.option-collisions.test.ts`

target.title: fix(tui): show busy startup loader during post-connect initialization [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## Summary

- **Problem:** During Terminal Hatch onboarding (and any local/gateway TUI connect), `client.onConnected` in `src/tui/tui.ts` flipped the connection status to `"local ready"`/`"connected"` immediately and then awaited post-connect initialization (`refreshAgents()`, `restoreRememberedSession()`, `loadHistory()`) without ever setting a busy **activity** status. `renderStatus()` only renders the spinner/loader when `isTuiBusyActivityStatus(activityStatus)` is true, and `"idle"` is not in that set — so no loader rendered while init ran. The status line read "ready" while the UI was actually still starting up, making the TUI look frozen/laggy for ~2s after each prompt during hatch.
- **Why it matters now:** This is a first-run onboarding responsiveness regression (`bug`, `regression`, P2) reported against Terminal Hatch. A prior fix PR (#f02f570b3f69) was closed unmerged because it introduced a startup-error rendering regression and lacked real behavior proof.
- **Intended outcome:** The TUI shows the busy status loader ("starting up") for the duration of post-connect init, then clears to the normal ready line once init actually finishes.
- **Out of scope:** Any underlying init latency optimization (the async work itself is unchanged); reconnect UX beyond reusing the same busy-state path.
- **Success:** Loader renders during onConnected init and clears on completion; the final ready state is byte-for-byte unchanged; startup-failure still renders the `"startup failed"` text (the prior PR's regression is avoided).
- **Reviewer focus:** The `onConnected` restructure in `src/tui/tui.ts` — specifically that the busy activity status is cleared on **both** the success path and the `.catch` startup-failure path (so the `"startup failed"` static status still renders), and that the post-init ready status is unchanged.

## Linked context

Closes #74385

Related: prior closed fix attempt f02f570b3f69 (closed unmerged — startup-error regression + missing real behavior proof).

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No — triaged from the `clawsweeper:queueable-fix` / `clawsweeper:source-repro` shortlist.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: TUI looks frozen/laggy for ~2s during Terminal Hatch onboarding because client.onConnected flips the status to "local ready" and runs async post-connect init (agent refresh, session restore, history load) without setting a busy activity status, so renderStatus() never shows the loader.
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu, ssh lxy-tx), Node v22.22.0, OpenClaw source tree at PR head 0a5b6eb8f2 (AFTER) and upstream main (BEFORE), driven through the real `runTui()`/`renderStatus()`/Loader render path under a real PTY (`src/tui/tui-pty-harness.e2e.test.ts` "shows a busy startup loader during post-connect initialization", with a slow post-connect init fixture so the loader window is visible). Also Windows 10 LTSC, Node v22.17.1 for the exported-helper reconnect-preservation check.

Did user-visible behavior change? **Yes** — intentionally. The TUI now shows a busy "starting up" loader during post-connect initialization instead of a falsely "ready" idle line. The final ready state is unchanged.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? **No.**

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? **No.** No CODEOWNERS secops paths touched.

What is the highest-risk area? The `client.onConnected` startup path, specifically that a thrown init error still renders the `"startup failed"` status text (the regression that sank the prior PR).

How is that risk mitigated? target.title: fix(gateway): preserve raw external session aliases
target.body:
Closes #63005.

## Behavior addressed

External raw session keys such as `conversation:pair:...` and opaque provider keys such as `Signal:Group:<mixed-case-id>` should survive gateway session-key canonicalization. Any follow-up mutation should keep the raw key and the visible `agent:<id>:` canonical key pointing at the same session entry instead of splitting history or plugin-owned state.

## Root cause

`migrateAndPruneGatewaySessionStoreKey` canonicalized raw external keys before preserving the raw-key store entry as an alias of the canonical agent key. The first fix preserved that raw alias, but some write paths still replaced, mutated, or deleted only one key.

The later review findings exposed the remaining gaps:

- checkpoint restore, checkpoint metadata, manual compaction, and maxLines compaction metadata paths still wrote only the canonical entry
- alias discovery lowercased opaque Signal group peer IDs
- after `sessions.list` hid the raw alias, canonical-key patch/delete/reset/compact flows did not rediscover the hidden raw alias
- plugin host-hook writers (`enqueuePluginNextTurnInjection`, `drainPluginNextTurnInjections`, and `patchPluginSessionExtension`) updated only `loaded.storeKey`, leaving hidden raw aliases with stale plugin state

The canonical-key derivation also has to preserve separators such as `user_a::user_b`, so it cannot use `parseAgentSessionKey` for raw-rest extraction because that parser drops empty segments.

## Fix

The preserved raw-alias logic is now shared in `src/gateway/session-store-aliases.ts`, with alias-aware write, sync, and delete helpers.

Covered mutation paths now route writes through the shared alias contract:

- `sessions.patch`
- `sessions.delete`
- `sessions.reset`
- agent writeback
- node-event store touches
- resolver sync
- `sessions.compaction.restore`
- compaction checkpoint metadata persistence
- `sessions.compact` manual metadata updates
- `sessions.compact` maxLines metadata updates
- plugin next-turn injection enqueue/drain
- plugin session-extension patch/unset

Preserved raw aliases stay internal-only for lookup continuity: `sessions.list` filtering/search/count collapses a raw+canonical alias pair into one visible canonical session row.

Canonical visible keys now rediscover an existing hidden raw alias by stripping the `agent:<id>:` prefix while preserving the rest of the key exactly. Canonical-only sessions do not grow a new raw alias.

Opaque Signal group peer IDs are preserved when deriving raw aliases, so mixed-case group IDs do not create lowercased duplicate logical session rows.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Raw external session aliases are preserved during canonicalization, stay synchronized across direct session mutations, compaction/checkpoint lifecycle writes, canonical visible-key follow-ups, and plugin host-hook writes, while keeping only one visible canonical row in list/search/count.

**Real environment tested:** Source checkout on PR head `1cde6d4a5d222273ed4c9c69b5d6e4ac402282c9`, base `f07c87405c3094feceaaf2f0f19a2e765a25e78d`, Node 22, repo dependencies installed.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
node --import tsx /private/tmp/pr83368-proof.ts
```

Also ran the targeted and broader regression commands listed in the Validation section below.

**Evidence after fix:**

```json
{

  "preservedAliasKeys": [
    "conversation:pair:user_a::user_b:space:space_123"
  ],
  "afterWrite": {
    "canonicalSessionId": "sess-write",
    "rawSessionId": "sess-write",
    "rawSendPolicy": "deny",
    "sameEntry": true
  },
  "visible": {
    "listKeys": [
      "agent:main:conversation:pair:user_a::user_b:space:space_123"
    ],
    "listCount": 1,
    "listTotalCount": 1,
    "searchKeys": [
      "agent:main:conversation:pair:user_a::user_b:space:space_123"
    ],
    "searchCount": 1,
    "searchTotalCount": 1
  },
  "deleted": true,
  "afterDelete": {
    "canonicalSessionId": null,
    "rawSessionId": null
  },
  "canonicalVisibleKeyFlow": {
    "listedKeys": [
      "agent:main:conversation:pair:user_a::user_b:space:space_123"
    ],
    "afterWrite": {
      "visibleKey": "agent:main:conversation:pair:user_a::user_b:space:space_123",
      "primaryKey": "agent:main:conversation:pair:user_a::user_b:space:space_123",

```

**Observed result after fix:** The raw alias and canonical key share the same written entry after replacement, including patched `sendPolicy`; list and search return one visible canonical row with `totalCount: 1`; delete removes both keys. Starting from the visible canonical list key also rediscovers the hidden raw alias, writes both aliases, and deletes both aliases. The plugin regressions show canonical-key plugin next-turn enqueue/drain and session-extension patch/unset update or clear the hidden raw alias too.

**What was not tested:** No full live external chat-channel round trip was run. No screenshots are attached because this is backend session-store behavior with no visual UI surface.

## Regression Coverage

- `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` covers raw/canonical alias collapse, mixed-case Signal opaque-ID preservation, canonical-key rediscovery, and canonical-only no-new-raw-alias behavior.

- `src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts` covers reset alias synchronization.

target.title: gateway: gate tool invoke until startup hooks are ready
target.body:
## Summary
- gate tools.invoke through the existing startup-unavailable method mechanism so tool invocation returns 503 while startup sidecars/plugins are still loading
- propagate unavailableGatewayMethods into the HTTP /tools/invoke path, covering direct HTTP in addition to RPC gateway methods
- preserve the gateway global hook runner when later scoped/default plugin runtime loads have fewer hooks, so startup-loaded security hooks remain active after readiness

## Why
OpenClaw binds the HTTP port before runtime-post-bind plugin startup completes. Before this patch, /tools/invoke could be accepted during that window while before_tool_call hooks were unavailable, causing a fail-open tool invocation path. This exists as a startup race, not a steady-state plugin failure.

## Verification
- pnpm test src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.test.ts src/gateway/server-http.request-trace.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods.control-plane-rate-limit.test.ts src/plugins/loader.test.ts src/plugins/providers.test.ts
- local live staging: fake tool race probe showed connection refused -> 503 plugins_not_ready -> 404 not_found
- local live prod after patch: fake tool race probe showed connection refused -> 503 plugins_not_ready -> 404 not_found; warm web_fetch to webhook.site returned 403 [T-EXFIL-003]

## Notes
The branch is based on current upstream main and contains only the focused readiness/hook-runner fix commits.

target.title: fix(telegram): move preview-streamed dedup to channel layer (#80520)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes the Telegram "reply appears briefly then disappears" regression reported in #80520. The previous core-layer dedup (#82625 / commit `bd51d8f2dd`) suppressed final payloads matching preview-streamed text but had no path to also signal the channel's `lane.finalized` state. When every final was suppressed (e.g., embedded harness + reasoning-model paragraph-split deliveries), the lane stayed unfinalized and the end-of-turn cleanup deleted the preview message.

This PR moves the dedup from the channel-agnostic core to the Telegram channel layer so the "skip duplicate send" and "mark lane finalized" steps happen atomically.

## Commits

1. **Revert "Deduplicate preview-streamed final replies (#82625)"** — undoes the previous dedup, which could not observe channel state.

2. **fix(telegram): move preview-streamed final dedup to channel layer (#80520)** — equivalent dedup at the channel layer:
   - New `extensions/telegram/src/preview-dedup.ts` helpers (whole + per-block normalization, exact-match check). 13 unit tests in `preview-dedup.test.ts`.
   - In `bot-message-dispatch.ts`, the dispatcher's `deliver` callback checks each text-only final against the answer lane's `lastPartialText`. On match: `answerLane.finalized = true`, `deliveryState.markDelivered()`, skip the send.
   - **Guards with a `previewMessageId` check** — only fires when the preview actually has an established Telegram message. If the preview never landed (e.g., transient failure), the final still flows through `sendPayload` so the user receives something. The previous core-layer dedup had no access to this state.
   - Media + caption payloads keep their existing path through `lane-delivery-text-deliverer.ts`'s `hasMedia` branch, which already handles caption stripping.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Telegram "reply appears briefly then disappears" regression for embedded-harness + reasoning-model + `streaming.mode=partial` paths (#80520).

Real environment tested: macOS, managed gateway service running this branch's `dist/`. Live Telegram bot configured with `model.primary = zai/glm-5.1` (reasoning model) via the embedded harness with `streaming.mode=partial`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `git checkout dev/telegram-preview-dedup && pnpm build` (build the patched `dist/`).
2. `openclaw gateway stop && openclaw gateway start` (run a live gateway on the patched build).
3. Sent a short (3-char) conversational message to the live agent through the Telegram client.
4. Sent an 80-char prompt asking the live agent to fetch and summarize an external URL; the model produced a 10-paragraph, ~1297-char markdown summary — the paragraph-split delivery shape this regression originally manifested on.
5. (Supplemental) Ran `pnpm test extensions/telegram` against the patched branch — 118 files, 1735 tests pass, including 4 new integration cases for the channel-layer dedup, the `previewMessageId` guard, multi-block deliveries, and error preservation.

Evidence after fix:

Redacted live `gateway.log` excerpt covering the 80-char inbound prompt and the subsequent long-reply turn on the live gateway (chat id and bot handle redacted as `<chat>` and `<bot>`; nothing else inside this turn was logged):

```
[telegram] Inbound message <chat> -> @<bot> (direct, 80 chars)
(no other [telegram] outbound line for this account between the inbound
 and 3 minutes later — no sendMessage, no deliverReplies, no
 editMessageTelegram from the channel adapter for this turn)
```

The absence of any outbound `[telegram]` line is the load-bearing observation from the live gateway: the 1297-char, 10-paragraph reply was delivered entirely through the existing preview-streaming `editMessageText` path on the already-established preview message id. On `main` without this PR, the previous `suppressPreviewStreamedPayloads` would have dropped each paragraph's final payload at the runner layer and `clearUnfinalizedStream` would have then deleted the preview message — the regression described in #80520.

Redacted live session jsonl excerpt for the same turn (assistant payload metadata as written by the running gateway; reply text and tool inputs/outputs omitted):

```json
{
  "type": "message",
  "message": {
    "role": "assistant",
    "provider": "zai",
    "model": "glm-5.1",
    "api": "openai-completions",
    "stopReason": "stop",
    "usage": {
      "input": 10445,
      "output": 585,
      "cacheRead": 130176,
      "totalTokens": 141206,
      "cost": { "input": 0.012534, "output": 0.00234, "cacheRead": 0.031242, "total": 0.046116 }
    },
    "content": [
      { "type": "text", "text": "<redacted: ~1297-char markdown reply with 10 paragraph blocks separated by blank lines>" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The same turn also wrote a `provider=openclaw, model=delivery-mirror` mirror entry ~11 s later with the same `content[0].text` value, confirming the channel side accepted the reply as delivered and finalized the lane — the cleanup did not fire and the preview message remained intact in the Telegram chat.

Before this PR on `main` (the parent of `56b09263ef`, before reverting `bd51d8f2dd`), the same setup repeatedly produced a preview message that flashed into the chat and disappeared without any visible final, matching the report on #80520. Reverting `bd51d8f2dd` alone restored delivery (with paragraph duplicates); this PR adds the channel-layer dedup that also removes the duplicates.

Observed result after fix:
- The 10-paragraph, ~1297-char live reply lands as a single Telegram chat bubble that contains every paragraph (not 10 separate messages) and stays in the chat permanently.
- No flashing/disappearing during or after streaming.
- No paragraph-split duplicates.
- Short conversational replies behave the same way (single message, stable).

What was not tested:
- Slack, MSTeams, Mattermost (the analogous dispatchers in those channels were not modified by this PR; whether they need similar treatment is follow-up work).
- Codex-harness paths (different code path, not affected by this PR).
- Live multi-instance / concurrent-turn scenarios.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test extensions/telegram` — 1735/1735 pass
- [x] Manual Telegram E2E with `zai/glm-5.1` embedded harness: short reply + 10-paragraph URL summary
- [ ] Maintainer to confirm whether Slack/MSTeams dispatchers need analogous treatment in a follow-up

Closes #80520.
